newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard criticises merger rules.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard criticises merger rules.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Tuesday criticised the country's anti-merger rules, saying they had prevented a sugar industry merger in 1993 that some experts had regarded as necessary.

"The government is somewhat concerned about rigidity of the the existing merger provisions of the Trade Practices Act, which were enacted by the former government in the face of opposition from the present government parties," Howard told parliament.

"And one of the consequence of those particular provisions of course has been to prevent greater rationalisation in the (sugar) industry which many observers of the industry regard as a necessary step forward, and I have in mind the rejection by the ACCC of the proposed merger between Mackay Sugar and CSR."
Howard commented on the merger rules in an announcement that Australia would drop its sugar import tariff.
In December 1993, the then Trade Practices Commission rejected a proposed merger between CSR Ltd, the Mackay Sugar Co-operative Association and British commodities house E D & F Man Group Plc.
The commission said at the time that economic gains from the merger would not offset the loss of competition that it would involve.
Section 50 of the Trade Practices Act prohibits mergers or acquisitions that substantially lessen competition in a substantial market for goods or services.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), which succeeded the Trade Practices Commission, is the government authority that enforces the provision.
